operator_io_quirks: All table names are mixed-case (Addresses, Products, Customers, Contacts, Customer_Address_History, Customer_Orders, Order_Items); DDL uses backticks, generated SQL must double-quote.
Tiny DB: every table has 15-20 rows; no huge-table sampling path exercised here.

DATETIME columns (date_from, date_to, order_date) store TEXT like '2015-07-23 14:37:18' (space separator, no T, no fractional seconds); declared type contains 'date' so TS dispatches to Date|Number(int elements) — first element is not int, so Date fuzzer with template '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'.
Customer_Address_History and Order_Items have NO primary key (pk=[]); upstream sample_fresh_primary_keys must no-op on empty PK, and drop_unique_duplicates has no unique columns to filter.
Order_Items.order_item_id is INTEGER NOT NULL but NOT a PK and NOT unique — it is a plain Number column, not a key.

FKs: Customer_Address_History -> Customers, Addresses; Customer_Orders -> Customers; Order_Items -> Customer_Orders, Products. All parents exist and are unique PKs; no dangling FKs, no self-references, no composite keys.
Contacts.customer_id is INTEGER NOT NULL with 9 distinct values over 15 rows (duplicates) but has NO declared FK to Customers — TS will treat it as a free Number column, not a FK.
gender VARCHAR(1) stores 'male'/'female' (length 4-6, exceeds declared length 1) — storage class text contradicts declared width; sqlite does not enforce VARCHAR length so inserts succeed.
order_quantity VARCHAR(80) mixes numeric strings ('3','7','9') with 'male' — String fuzzer will see int-like elements and add str(i±1) variants plus contaminated strings.
product_price DOUBLE stores huge reals (5.4e7, 3.0e7) — Number fuzzer with scale=4 gives range [-10^4,10^4], so fresh draws are far smaller than originals; list range quirk (min(el), 10^4) applies.
zip_postcode / customer_number are VARCHAR storing short numeric strings ('740','041','456') — String fuzzer int-like branch adds ±1 variants; leading-zero strings ('041') may be perturbed.
country has distinct=1 ('USA'); state_province_county distinct=14; product_type_code/payment_method_code/order_status_code distinct=2 — low-cardinality ENUM-like columns.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on date_from/date_to/order_date: template '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', range from min/max of 5 sampled originals; fresh draws uniform in that range, so dates stay plausible but lose the original's clustering (date_to clustered in 2018-03).
Number fuzzer on *_id INTEGER PKs: scale=4, range [-10^4,10^4], int perturbation ±1/±2; PKs will be small ints, not the original 1..15 — joins still work because FKs draw from parent's final values.

Number fuzzer on product_price DOUBLE: scale=4 -> fresh draws in [-10^4,10^4], far below originals (1e7); list-range quirk (min(el), 10^4) means even 'element' branch is bounded by 10^4 — likely FN on price-threshold queries.

String fuzzer on names/cities/addresses: fresh random strings over a-zA-Z0-9() of length 0-20 (or declared length), plus 50% contamination; original names like 'Kayley' will be replaced by gibberish — FN on LIKE/name-equality queries, FP on queries that only check non-null.

String fuzzer on low-cardinality ENUMs (product_type_code, payment_method_code, order_status_code, gender): 5 sampled originals + pool values, p=0.2 fresh; contamination may produce 'Hardwarex' etc. — FN on exact-match, FP on 'not in' style.

String fuzzer on customer_phone/contact_phone: originals have varied formats ('+87(9)...', '896.685.8228x2786', '(192)144-4687'); fresh strings are random charset — FN on phone-format queries, FP on length/prefix checks.
String fuzzer on customer_email: originals are 'x@example.com'; fresh strings lack '@' — FN on email-pattern queries.

FK columns (Customer_Address_History.customer_id/address_id, Customer_Orders.customer_id, Order_Items.order_id/product_id) draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement — referential integrity holds, but cardinality of distinct FK values may differ from original (9 distinct customer_id over 15 rows).

Contacts.customer_id (no FK) is a free Number column — TS will NOT tie it to Customers.customer_id, so joins Contacts-Customers may return fewer/more rows than original — likely FP/FN on join-count queries.
Order_Items has no PK: sample_fresh_primary_keys no-ops, so duplicate (order_id, product_id) pairs are allowed — FP on DISTINCT/count queries that assume uniqueness.
order_quantity mixes '3' and 'male': String fuzzer's int-like branch adds '4','2' etc., contamination adds suffixes — FN on numeric-cast queries, FP on 'male' equality.

Tiny tables (15-20 rows): choose_table_sizes level-0 = 1+30*u (1-31 rows) or rand_lin 30+int(u*200) (30-230) — generated instances are 1-15x larger than original, so count-based queries will differ — FP on exact-count, FN on 'no rows' predicates.
